subject: Culture
title: Internet Slang Evolution
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Internet Slang Evolution.

hook.text: 'LOL' entered the Oxford English Dictionary in 2011. It started in a 1989 chat room.

buildup.text: Internet slang evolves at hyperspeed. 'Skibidi' and 'rizz' went from zero to millions of uses in months.

discovery.text: Linguist Gretchen McCulloch calls internet language the largest natural experiment in writing ever conducted.

twist.text: Typing 'haha' vs 'hahaha' vs 'lol' vs 'lmao' signals precise social positioning. Length encodes sincerity.

climax.text: Teenagers instinctively read period marks as hostile. Punctuation has been repurposed as emotional markup.

punchline.text: The internet didn't kill grammar. It invented new grammar.

quiz.question: According to Gretchen McCulloch, what is internet language?

details.summary: Internet slang evolves faster than any language phenomenon in history — LOL, YOLO, 'slay,' 'bussin,' 'no cap' emerge and fade within months. Meme language creates in-group identities.
details.whyItMatters: Internet slang evolution reveals how language change has accelerated from centuries to months. It also exposes ongoing patterns of cultural appropriation from marginalized communities.
takeaways: Internet slang cycles through invention, adoption, and death in months
AAVE is the primary source of mainstream American internet slang
Meme language creates in-group identity and out-group confusion

faq.question: Why does internet slang change so fast?
faq.answer: Internet slang changes fast because it functions as social currency — once a term becomes mainstream, it loses its in-group signaling value. 'Cool' lasted decades because media spread slowly. 'YOLO' lasted months because virality is instantaneous.

faq.question: Why is AAVE so influential in internet slang?
faq.answer: African American Vernacular English is linguistically creative, culturally expressive, and regularly produces innovative vocabulary. White and non-Black internet users adopt AAVE terms (slay, lit, woke, cap, bussin) through social media exposure, often without understanding their origin.
